intro: A straight-line model misses a curved trend. Change its feature representation while keeping prediction linear in the learned weights.
task: Build a polynomial design matrix whose columns are 1, x, x squared, through x to the requested degree.
requirements: x is a nonempty finite vector. degree is an integer from 1 through 5; booleans are invalid.
Return a NumPy matrix with len(x) rows and degree + 1 columns, in ascending power order.
The first column is always one, including for zero or negative inputs.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Broadcast x[:, None] against an array of exponents starting at zero.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: A degree of two produces three columns because the intercept feature is included.

explanation: A linear model is linear in its coefficients, not necessarily in the original input. The feature map [1, x, x²] lets a weighted sum describe a parabola.
Column order matters because every coefficient is attached to a particular power. An ascending Vandermonde matrix makes that convention explicit.
Compare the magnitudes of x and x⁵ for a large input. Richer features can make optimization poorly conditioned; adding powers is a modeling choice, not a guarantee of better generalization.
